challenges.name: versioned-prompts-quiz
challenges.title: Prompts as versioned templates
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the hint feature: a renderer that replaces one variable after another, and a prompt change rolled out as a new version.

questions.explanation: False. The first replaceAll puts the learner's code into the template. The second replaceAll then scans the whole string again, the inserted code included, so the comment becomes "// TODO: print Sum of an array in the header". The model now reads code the learner never wrote. A renderer must read the template once and insert each value without scanning it again, because learner code is untrusted input and can contain anything, template syntax included. (A string passed as the replacement to replace or replaceAll has a second trap: "$&" and "$'" in it are replacement patterns.) The misconception is that replacing variables one after another is the same as rendering once. It is the same only while no value contains placeholder syntax, and you do not control the values.

FROM hint_responses WHERE created_at > now() - interval '2 days'
GROUP BY prompt_ref;

Statement: "To go back to the old prompt, setting active back to hint-v3@3 is enough, and the same query will then show whether the thumbs-down rate returns to its earlier level."
questions.explanation: True. Version 3 was released and never edited, so its text is still in the repository exactly as it ran. Rolling back is a one-line config change, not a hunt through git history for the old wording. Because every stored hint carries prompt_ref, the query separates the answers of each version, and after the rollback new rows arrive as hint-v3@3 again. When you compare, look at similar traffic (same days, same challenges), because the mix of learners and challenges changes the rate too. The misconception is that a prompt change can be edited in place and judged by the date of the deploy. With in-place edits, two different texts share one name, and nothing in the data tells them apart.

challenges.name: render-versioned-prompt
challenges.title: Render a versioned prompt template
challenges.description: The CodeDev hint service builds its prompt from the template hint-v3 (version 3). The old renderer, `text.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (_, k) => String(vars[k]))`, put the word "undefined" into the prompt when a variable was renamed, logged no version, and treated `{{...}}` inside learner code as template syntax. Write renderPrompt(template, variables) for template = { id, version, text } and variables = an object of values parsed from JSON. Return { ok: true, ref, prompt, warnings } or { ok: false, ref, errors, warnings }. Rules: (1) ref is "<id>@<version>", for example "hint-v3@3", on every result. (2) Read text once, from left to right. A backslash followed by {{ (the three characters \{{) is an escape: write a literal {{ and continue after it. {{ followed by a name and }} is a placeholder; a name is a letter (A-Z, a-z) followed by letters, digits or underscores, with no spaces. Any other {{ is an error "malformed placeholder at <index>", where index is the 0-based position of that {{ in text; continue scanning right after those two braces. All other characters (a single {, a }} on its own, a backslash not followed by {{) are copied as they are. (3) A placeholder whose variable is a string is replaced by that string; a number is replaced by String(value). Anything else (no such key, null, true or false, an object, an array) is an error "missing variable: <name>", reported once per name, at its first occurrence. An empty string and 0 are values. (4) Insert values exactly as given and never scan them again: {{...}}, \{{ and $& inside a value stay as they are. (5) errors are in the order the scan finds them. If there is at least one error, return ok: false with all of them and no prompt. (6) warnings: "unused variable: <name>" for every key of variables that no placeholder in the template uses (a malformed placeholder uses nothing), sorted by name (the default string sort), on both kinds of result. The runner reads a list of { template, variables } and prints the list of results as JSON.
hints: If you replace the placeholders one variable at a time, what happens when the learner's code itself contains "{{challengeTitle}}"? What would a renderer have to do so that a value is never looked at a second time?

Walk through text with an index and build the output in a separate string. At each position there are only three cases to check, in this order: does the text start with \{{ here, does it start with {{ here, or is it a plain character? For the {{ case, a regular expression with the sticky flag (/.../y) and lastIndex = i tests a name and the closing braces at exactly that position. Keep a Set of used names (for the warnings) and a Set of names already reported as missing.

A similar scan on a different syntax, ${name} with $${ as the escape, for the text "Hi ${user}, cost $${x} ${user}" and variables { user: "Ann", unused: 1 }: at index 3 the text starts with ${ and the name user is followed by } -> append "Ann", add user to used, jump past the closing brace. At index 15 the text starts with $${ -> append "${" and jump 3 characters. The rest is copied. Result: "Hi Ann, cost ${x} Ann", warnings ["unused variable: unused"]. If user had been null, the result would instead be one error, "missing variable: user", even though user appears twice.
